details:
Implementation Plan

Plan for `docs/plans/apply-ai-tools-learnings-plan.md` Phases 1–2, scoped to this issue only.

Ref context
- Commit: `fc9049673fdeeec58b291d0998d3af6e78834f8e`
- Branch: `orchestrator/project-3024`
- Integration metadata match: yes

Clarification interpretation
- No clarification questions were asked.
- `/answer [auto-answered-by-orchestrator]` adds no new constraints, so planning proceeds from the issue body as written.

Automation / wiring summary
- Change type: modify one existing file only.
- Scheduler / PR-push wiring: none.
- New supervisor: none.
- DB gate pattern: n/a.
- `docs/scripts-pending-removal.md`: no entry needed.

1. Files likely to change
- `unattended_system_instructions.md` only.
- No creates, deletes, or renames.
- All edits are additive except the existing §4 shell-write verification bullet, which is refined in place.
- No workflow, script, prompt, README, or `CLAUDE.md` changes in this issue.

2. Functions / modules / sections to implement
Treat the numbered sections in `unattended_system_instructions.md` as the implementation units.

- `§2. Bias to Action` (current lines ~81–92)
  - Append one new anti-laziness paragraph after the current `BLOCKED:` paragraph and before the `---`.
  - Use the Phase 1 wording from the source-of-truth plan, ending with: “Either emit the artefact or emit `BLOCKED:` with a scalar reason.”

- `§3. Tool-Call Discipline (codex paths)` (current lines ~98–111)
  - Insert a new XML-style block named `<status_update_cadence>` before the section separator.
  - Follow the formatting pattern already used by `<tool_persistence_rules>` and `<verification_loop>`.
  - The new block must cover:
    - one short preamble sentence (≤20 words) before each tool-call batch;
    - a compact `Checkpoint:` after every 3–5 tool calls, or after any edit burst touching more than 3 files since the last checkpoint;
    - preambles/checkpoints go to stdout/logs and do not replace the §16 terminal summary or count as the artefact.

- `§4. Edit-Tool Discipline (codex paths)` (current lines ~127–129)
  - Refine the existing bullet so it explicitly applies to shell writes only (`heredoc`, `printf`, redirected `cat`, `tee`).
  - Add the sibling `apply_patch` rule from the source-of-truth plan:
    - no reread after a successful `apply_patch`;
    - end-of-rollout verification still happens via `git diff --stat` across the edited files.

- `§9. Minimal Change Set` (after current line ~187)
  - Append the new final bullet with the “default mode is surgical” wording from the source-of-truth plan, including the rule that ambiguity defaults to surgical, never ambitious.

- `§15. Role-Specific Behavior` (current role paragraphs at ~295–310)
  - Append the same root-cause sentence to:
    - `Editor (review autofix)`
    - `Implementer (implement)`
    - `Diagnoser / Judge`
  - Keep the sentence identical in all 3 places for grepability.

- `§16. Output Contract`
  - Add one new outer bullet to the existing list requiring user-visible artefacts to describe actions in natural language rather than tool names.
  - Add one new bullet inside the existing `<verification_loop>` with the ordered executable-check tiers:
    - `typecheck → lint → tests → build → smoke`
    - stop at the first failing tier.

- Acceptance alignment
  - Keep all existing section numbers and headings unchanged.
  - Keep all existing XML tag names unchanged.
  - The only new tag is `<status_update_cadence>`.
  - Final diff stays limited to `unattended_system_instructions.md`.

3. Data structures affected
- No runtime data structures.
- Prompt-contract structures only:
  - new internal XML-style block: `<status_update_cadence>`;
  - existing `<verification_loop>` gains one bullet;
  - existing role paragraphs and bullet lists gain additive text.
- No env vars, log prefixes, identifiers, or DB contracts change.

4. API / interface changes
- No public API or workflow interface changes.
- Internal behavioral contract changes only, affecting phases that consume `unattended_system_instructions.md`:
  - artefact-producing phases must emit the artefact or `BLOCKED:`;
  - user-visible artefacts should avoid tool-name wording;
  - verification guidance gains an explicit tier order;
  - stdout/log cadence gains preambles/checkpoints.

5. Potential risks / edge cases
- Keep the new `<status_update_cadence>` block inside §3, before the `---`.
- Keep the new verification-order bullet inside the existing `<verification_loop>` block, not after it.
- Do not weaken the existing verification rule in §4:
  - shell writes still require immediate diff verification;
  - `apply_patch` still gets end-of-rollout diff verification.
- Avoid unrelated prose reflow in adjacent sections.
- Keep the root-cause sentence identical in all three roles.
- Conflict to note:
  - `prompts/mode-implement.txt:31-33` conditionally allows editing `unattended_system_instructions.md` when the approved plan scopes it.
  - `.github/workflows/implement.yml:1510` still unconditionally says not to modify `ai_pipeline.md, unattended_system_instructions.md, or CLAUDE.md`.
  - That conflicts with the issue note that the unlock dependency is in place. Treat the separate unlock issue as a prerequisite/rebase dependency; do not widen this issue to change workflow or prompt files.

6. Testing considerations
- Scope check: `git diff --stat -- unattended_system_instructions.md` should show only this file.
- Manual diff review should confirm:
  - all six requested additions landed;
  - §4 is the only refined-in-place edit;
  - no section renumbering or tag renaming occurred.
- Spot checks:
  - `<status_update_cadence>` appears once;
  - the root-cause sentence appears in exactly 3 role paragraphs;
  - the tool-name-opacity bullet is in §16’s outer list;
  - the verification-order bullet is inside `<verification_loop>`.
- Optional post-merge smoke:
  - run one small unattended implement/review cycle and confirm logs show preambles/checkpoints and user-visible artefacts avoid tool-name phrasing.

Assumption
- The implement-prompt unlock dependency is merged into `orchestrator/project-3024` before implementation starts; otherwise this single-file plan is correct but the live implement workflow may still block the edit.

Estimated effort
- ~25–35 minutes once the unlock dependency is present, so this should fit within the one-rollout (~55 minute) target.
